arxiv-1702-01209.title: Probabilistic Sensor Fusion for Ambient Assisted Living Journal: Information Fusion
arxiv-1702-01209.creator: Tom Diethe, Niall Twomey, Meelis Kull, Peter Flach, Ian Craddock
arxiv-1702-01209.description: Abstract There is a widely-accepted need to revise current forms of health-care provision, with particular interest in sensing systems in the home. Given a multiple-modality sensor platform with heterogeneous network connectivity, as is under development in the SPHERE ( SPHERE ) IRC ( IRC ), we face specific challenges relating to the fusion of the heterogeneous sensor modalities.

arxiv-1803-07708.title: K2 Ultracool Dwarfs Survey. III. White Light Flares are Ubiquitous in M6-L0 Dwarfs Facilities: Kepler astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , emcee ( Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 )
arxiv-1803-07708.creator: Rishi R. Paudel, John E. Gizis, D. J. Mullan, Sarah J. Schmidt, Adam J. Burgasser, Peter K. G. Williams, Edo Berger
arxiv-1803-07708.description: Abstract We report the white light flare rates for 10 ultracool dwarfs (UCDs) using Kepler K2 short cadence data. Among our sample stars, two have spectral type M6, three are M7, three are M8 and two are L0. Most of our targets are old low mass stars.

arxiv-2012-07596.title: Biomechanical modelling of brain atrophy through deep learning
arxiv-2012-07596.creator: Mariana da Silva, Kara Garcia, Carole H. Sudre, Cher Bass, M. Jorge Cardoso, Emma Robinson
arxiv-2012-07596.description: Abstract We present a proof-of-concept, deep learning (DL) based, differentiable biomechanical model of realistic brain deformations. Using prescribed maps of local atrophy and growth as input, the network learns to deform images according to a Neo-Hookean model of tissue deformation.

arxiv-2101-03162.title: Bit Error Rate Analysis for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces with Phase Errors Thanks: I. Trigui, E. K. Agbogla, and W. Ajib are with the Département d’informatique, Université du Québec à Montréal, Montreal, Canada. E-mails: trigui.imen@courrier.uqam.ca, agbogla.komi_edouard@courrier.uqam.ca, an
arxiv-2101-03162.creator: Imène Trigui, Edouard Komi Agbogla, Mustapha Benjillali
arxiv-2101-03162.description: Abstract In this paper, we analyze the error probability of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS)-enabled communication systems with quantized channel phase compensation over Rayleigh fading channels. The probability density and characteristic functions of the received signal amplitude are derived and used to compute exact expressions for the bit error rate (BER).

arxiv-2310-16524.title: Can You Rely on Your Model Evaluation? Improving Model Evaluation with Synthetic Test Data
arxiv-2310-16524.creator: Boris van BreugelUniversity of Cambridge bv292@cam.ac.uk, Nabeel SeedatUniversity of Cambridge ns741@cam.ac.uk Fergus ImrieUCLA imrie@g.ucla.edu Mihaela van der SchaarUniversity of Cambridge mv472@cam.ac.uk
arxiv-2310-16524.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Boris van BreugelUniversity of Cambridge bv292@cam.ac.uk, Nabeel SeedatUniversity of Cambridge ns741@cam.ac.uk Fergus ImrieUCLA imrie@g.ucla.edu Mihaela van der SchaarUniversity of Cambridge mv472@cam.ac.uk. Evaluating the performance of machine learning models on diverse and underrepresented subgroups is essential for ensuring fairness and reliability in real-world applications. However, accurately assessing model performance becomes challenging due to two main issues: (1) a scarcity of test data, especially for small subgroups, and (2) possible distributional shifts in the model’s deployment setting, which may not align with the available test data.

arxiv-2403-05549.title: A Scheduling Perspective on Modular Educational Systems in Europe Journal: International Journal of Educational Research
arxiv-2403-05549.creator: Rubén Ruiz-Torrubiano, Sebastian Knopp, Lukas Matthias Wolf, Andreas Krystallidis
arxiv-2403-05549.description: Abstract In modular educational systems, students are allowed to choose a part of their own curriculum themselves. This is typically done in the final class levels which lead to maturity for university access. The rationale behind letting students choose their courses themselves is to enhance self-responsibility, improve student motivation, and allow a focus on specific areas of interest.

arxiv-2408-11338.title: Automatic Dataset Construction (ADC): Sample Collection, Data Curation, and Beyond
arxiv-2408-11338.creator: Minghao Liu, Zonglin Di, Jiaheng Wei, Zhongruo Wang, Hengxiang Zhang, Ruixuan Xiao Haoyu Wang, Jinlong Pang, Hao Chen, Ankit Shah, Hongxin Wei, Xinlei He Zhaowei Zhu, Haobo Wang, Lei Feng, Jindong Wang, James Davis, Yang Liu University of California, Santa Cruz Amazon SUSTech Zhejiang University Yal
arxiv-2408-11338.description: Abstract Large-scale data collection is essential for developing personalized training data, mitigating the shortage of training data, and fine-tuning specialized models. However, creating high-quality datasets quickly and accurately remains a challenge due to annotation errors, the substantial time and costs associated with human labor.

arxiv-2411-19134.title: Visual SLAMMOT Considering Multiple Motion Models
arxiv-2411-19134.creator: Peilin Tian, Hao Li
arxiv-2411-19134.description: Abstract Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) and Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) are pivotal tasks in the realm of autonomous driving, attracting considerable research attention. While SLAM endeavors to generate real-time maps and determine the vehicle’s pose in unfamiliar settings, MOT focuses on the real-time identification and tracking of multiple dynamic objects.

arxiv-2509-21467.title: Radio Stars in the Era of New Observatories
arxiv-2509-21467.creator: Lynn D. Matthews
arxiv-2509-21467.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lynn D. Matthews. An international conference Radio Stars in the Era of New Observatories was held at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology Haystack Observatory on 2024 April 17–19. The conference brought together more than 60 researchers from around the world, united by an interest in using radio wavelength observations to explore the physical processes that operate in stars (including the Sun), how stars evolve and interact with their environments, and the role of radio stars as probes of our Galaxy.

arxiv-2510-19022.title: MoAlign: Motion-Centric Representation Alignment for Video Diffusion Models Thanks: Qualcomm AI Research is an initiative of Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.
arxiv-2510-19022.creator: Aritra Bhowmik, Denis Korzhenkov, Cees G. M. Snoek, Amirhossein Habibian, Mohsen Ghafoorian
arxiv-2510-19022.description: Abstract Text-to-video diffusion models have enabled high-quality video synthesis, yet often fail to generate temporally coherent and physically plausible motion. A key reason is the models’ insufficient understanding of complex motions that natural videos often entail. Recent works tackle this problem by aligning diffusion model features with those from pretrained video encoders.

We have quantified the variance in...

pmc-10594701.title: Anticancer perspective of 6-shogaol: anticancer properties, mechanism of action, synergism and delivery system
pmc-10594701.creator: Yaoxia Jia, Xing Li, Xiangqi Meng, Jinjie Lei, Yangmiao Xia, Lingying Yu
pmc-10594701.description: Cancer is a malignant disease that has plagued human beings all the time, but the treatment effect of commonly used anticancer drugs in clinical practice is not ideal by reason of their drug tolerance and Strong adverse reactions to patients. Therefore, it is imperative to find effective and low-toxic anticancer drugs.

pmc-10612513.title: A Progressively Disassembled DNA Repair Inhibitors Nanosystem for the Treatment of BRCA Wild-Type Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
pmc-10612513.creator: Weimin Fang, Jinghao Wang, Xiaocong Ma, Ni Shao, Kunlin Ye, Dong Zhang, Changzheng Shi, Liangping Luo
pmc-10612513.description: BackgroundOlaparib, a poly (adenosine diphosphate-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitor has demonstrated promising efficacy in patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) carrying breast cancer gene (BRCA) mutations. However, its impact on BRCA wild-type (BRCAwt) TNBC is limited. Hence, it is crucial to sensitize BRCAwt TNBC cells to olaparib for effective clinical practice.

pmc-10631727.title: XPF interacts with TOP2B for R-loop processing and DNA looping on actively transcribed genes
pmc-10631727.creator: Georgia Chatzinikolaou, Kalliopi Stratigi, Athanasios Siametis, Evi Goulielmaki, Alexia Akalestou-Clocher, Ioannis Tsamardinos, Pantelis Topalis, Caroline Austin, Britta A. M. Bouwman, Nicola Crosetto, Janine Altmüller, George A. Garinis
pmc-10631727.description: Co-transcriptional RNA-DNA hybrids can not only cause DNA damage threatening genome integrity but also regulate gene activity in a mechanism that remains unclear. Here, we show that the nucleotide excision repair factor XPF interacts with the insulator binding protein CTCF and the cohesin subunits SMC1A and SMC3, leading to R-loop–dependent DNA looping upon transcription activation.

pmc-10742854.title: Involuntary Treatment for Child and Adolescent Anorexia Nervosa—A Narrative Review and Possible Advances to Move Away from Coercion
pmc-10742854.creator: Ingar M Zielinski-Gussen, Beate Herpertz-Dahlmann, Brigitte Dahmen, Lene Lauge Berring, Eugenie Georgaca
pmc-10742854.description: Background: Children and adolescents with psychiatric disorders frequently experience hospital treatment as coercive. In particular, for patients with severe anorexia nervosa (AN), clinical and ethical challenges often arise if they do not voluntarily agree to hospital admission, often due to the ego-syntonic nature of the disorder. In these cases, involuntary treatment (IVT) might be life-saving.

pmc-11325566.title: Testing the validity of the Norwegian translation of the modified weight bias internalization scale
pmc-11325566.creator: Tiffany Lussier, Jon Harald Quindao Tangen, Trine Tetlie Eik-Nes, Håvard R Karlsen, Kjersti Hognes Berg, Charlotte Fiskum
pmc-11325566.description: BackgroundIndividuals with higher weight (overweight or obesity) may experience social stigma due to their weight. Weight stigma can be internalized with adverse health effects. Internalized weight stigma is relevant across different weight categories, but no validated weight-neutral measure of internalized weight bias currently exists in Norway.

pmc-11508929.title: Comparison of Croup Management Patterns between Pediatricians and Emergency Medicine Physicians: A Single Pediatric Emergency Department Study
pmc-11508929.creator: Ho-Young Song, Jae-Hyun Kwon, Soo Hyun Park, Min-Jung Kim, Young-Hoon Byun, So-Hyun Paek, Javier De Miguel Díez
pmc-11508929.description: Background/Objectives: With the advent of the field of pediatric emergency medicine, studies on the differences in treatment patterns between pediatricians and emergency medicine (EM) physicians in various pediatric conditions have been accumulating. This study aimed to compare croup (acute laryngotracheobronchitis) management patterns between pediatricians and EM physicians to enhance pediatric emergency care and inform the training of future specialists.

pmc-11658121.title: Exploring the relaxation effects of Coptis chinensis and berberine on the lower esophageal sphincter: potential strategies for LES motility disorders
pmc-11658121.creator: Wen-Harn Koh, Li-Wei Lin, Ting-I Lin, Ching-Wen Liu, Li-Ching Chang, I-Chun Lin, Ming-Shiang Wu, Ching-Chung Tsai
pmc-11658121.description: BackgroundEsophageal achalasia, a primary disorder impacting the lower esophageal sphincter (LES), presents symptoms such as dysphagia, regurgitation, chest pain, and weight loss. Traditional treatments, including calcium channel blockers and nitrates, offer limited relief, prompting exploration into alternative therapies. This study examines the efficacy of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), focusing on Coptis chinensis (C.

pmc-11712605.title: Racial/Ethnic Differences in Physical Activity Participation of Dementia Caregivers in the US: Findings from the 2017 BRFSS Survey
pmc-11712605.creator: Jiaming Liang
pmc-11712605.description: BackgroundIt is well documented that participating in physical activity can help dementia caregivers alleviate stress and enhance well‐being. However, few studies have examined dementia caregivers’ needs for exercise, and the feasibility of promoting their physical activity amidst heavy caregiving responsibilities.

pmc-11815964.title: Factors Influencing the Amount of ACL Remnant Available for Preservation at the Time of ACL Surgery
pmc-11815964.creator: Alessandro Carrozzo, Mohammed Lahsika, Christian Lattermann, Adnan Saithna, Jae-Sung An, Giancarlo Giurazza, Silvia Cardarelli, Thais Dutra Vieira, Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet
pmc-11815964.description: Background:The preservation of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) remnant during reconstruction or repair could offer advantages such as enhanced vascularity, proprioception, and biomechanical properties. However, research on the clinical factors influencing ACL remnant preservation at the time of surgery is limited.Purpose/Hypothesis:The purpose was to identify clinical factors influencing the amount of ACL remnant during surgery.
